critical_issues: CRITICAL (A/B FAIRNESS — the GEMV-vs-GEMM trap, inverted from M3.4's honest loss): the design's HEADLINE / kill-criterion-of-record metric (OQ-1 option A, technical_spec §3 option A, design_md_additions) compares AXIOM's FUSED GEMM TFLOPS against llama.cpp's n==1 GEMV TFLOPS (7.39). This is apples-to-oranges in ARITHMETIC INTENSITY, not just shape: a GEMM amortizes the weight load over n output columns and is structurally far easier to make fast per-FLOP than a memory-bound n==1 GEMV. The pinned llama.cpp raw output (.pipeline/benchmarks/m34/llamacpp_raw.txt) PROVES this: the SAME llama.cpp Q4_K MUL_MAT at n=512 runs at 101.00 TFLOPS vs 7.39 at n=1 — a 13.7x intensity-driven difference on the IDENTICAL kernel. The architect's own OQ-4 estimate puts the AXIOM fused GEMM at ~10-25 TFLOPS. So option A would let AXIOM print 'roughly 1-3x AHEAD of llama' (the architect literally writes 'AXIOM possibly AHEAD on TFLOPS') while the honest same-shape number (AXIOM-GEMM vs llama's n=512 GEMM = 101 TFLOPS) shows AXIOM at ~10-25% — i.e. 4-10x BEHIND. Making the GEMV-boundary the headline + the kill-criterion-of-record FLATTERS AXIOM by ~13x. This is precisely the apples-to-oranges the M3.4 harness was built to avoid; M3.4 was honest ONLY because both sides were matvec/GEMV (same low intensity). REQUIRED: the kill-criterion-of-record number MUST be the SAME-SHAPE comparison (AXIOM fused GEMM vs llama's Q4_K MUL_MAT at the SAME (m,n,k), e.g. n=512 at 101 TFLOPS, or AXIOM matvec vs llama n=1 GEMV). Option B must be promoted from 'honest secondary' to the kill-criterion-of-record; option A (GEMV-boundary) may appear ONLY as explicitly-labeled cross-shape context, never as the headline ratio or the within-15% verdict input.

CRITICAL (NUMERICS ORACLE does NOT match the GPU's accumulation precision): the GPU coopmat accumulator is f16 (matmul_rb_coopmat.axc lines 122-125: `matrix[f16, 16, 16, accumulator]`, reused verbatim per design_principle 1), but the proposed CPU oracle (common_q4km_f16ref.rs::q4km_dequant_matmul_f16weights_cpu) ACCUMULATES IN f32 (correctness_oracle: 'matmul accumulate in f32'). An f32-accumulator reference is NOT a 'tight upper bound' on an f16-accumulator kernel's error as the spec claims — it is a DIFFERENT computation. f16 has ~3 decimal digits; summing K=512 f16 products (32 K-blocks each contributing a 16-deep f16 partial sum inside the tensor core, then 32 f16 cross-block adds) accumulates rounding the f32 reference never sees. The spec's correctness_oracle asserts '1e-3 budget covers the f16-accumulator rounding for the tested sizes (K<=512)' but provides NO derivation — OQ-2 admits this is unconfirmed and punts the gate-K to reviewers. The hazard is that the Coder, to make AT-1771 (K=512) pass, LOOSENS 1e-3 to force a pass — a numerics goalpost-move. REQUIRED: either (a) make the reference accumulate in f16 to MATCH the GPU's actual accumulation precision (the honest oracle), or (b) keep the f32-accumulator reference but DERIVE/MEASURE the largest K at which 1e-3-relative provably holds, gate within-tol ONLY at that K, and report larger-K divergence SEPARATELY and HONESTLY (not by loosening the tolerance). The 1e-3 tolerance is FROZEN at the M2.6/M3.1 value (AT-1520/AT-1521) and MUST NOT be relaxed to absorb f16-accumulator error.
warnings: WARNING (f16-accumulator note in the oracle is internally inconsistent): the spec says the GPU accumulator is f16 AND that the f32-accumulator reference is a 'tight upper bound'. If the f32-ref is genuinely a tight bound at K<=512, the design should SHOW the measured max-rel-diff headroom under 1e-3, not assert it. If it is not, AT-1771 will fail or the tolerance will be pushed. Demand the Coder REPORT the measured max-rel-diff at K=256 and K=512 in the test output (not just assert <=1e-3) so the headroom is visible and a future larger-K frontier is documented.

WARNING (OQ-4 ALU-bound honesty): the dequant recomputes get_scale_min_k4 + d/dmin per element across all 32 lanes for every tile_k=16 K-block (16x redundant within a superblock, OQ-3). If the kernel is ALU-bound (dequant dominates) it will NOT reach coopmat throughput and may land well below M3.3c's 31.2 TFLOPS. This is acknowledged (OQ-4) and gated honestly (improvement over 0.000085 TFLOPS, no asserted TFLOPS) — acceptable, BUT only if the A/B verdict (Critical #1) is same-shape; a flattering GEMV-boundary headline would HIDE the ALU-bound deficit behind an intensity-mismatched comparison.

WARNING (superblock-to-tile staging coverage, AT-1620 class): the new dequant-into-shared replaces the M3.3c a_iter staging loop. Each a_tile element (ei_a = a_iter*32 + lane, 16 iters x 32 lanes = 512 elements) must be written EXACTLY ONCE with the correct dequantized weight. The superblock-to-tile index mapping (sb=k/256, chunk=(k%256)/64, l=(k%64)%32, nibble by (k%64)>=32) is recomputed per element from a_global_row*K + a_global_col — verify NO element is skipped or double-written, and that the lo/hi nibble + sub-block selection (is=chunk*2+(hi?1:0)) matches the FROZEN q4km_dequant_matmul.axc byte-identical logic. AT-1770 (K=256, 1 superblock) and AT-1771 (K=512, 2 superblocks) must include a coverage assertion, not just an end-to-end tolerance check, to catch a partial-staging bug masked by a lucky tolerance pass.

WARNING (m34_emit.py reuse): the existing emit.py hard-codes ratio = axc_tflops_sustained / llama_tflops where llama_tflops is parsed from the n==1 line only (harness line 130 greps ',n=1,'). Adding M34_AXC_KERNEL=fused without ALSO parsing a same-shape llama line (n=512) means the --fused path would STILL divide AXIOM-GEMM by llama-n1-GEMV — silently producing the flattering number. The same-shape llama line MUST be parsed and used for the kill-criterion (ties to Critical #1).
principle_violations: No NEW principle violation in the f32_to_f16 builtin itself: it is a genuine language gap (SharedWriteTypeMismatch at typecheck.rs:3540 requires exact f16 RHS, no coercion — confirmed; AXIOM has only f16_bits_to_f32 + f32_from_u32, no f32->f16 — confirmed in q4_0.rs). The builtin keeps explicitness (anti-pattern #1: still an explicit named call, no implicit coercion). Acceptable.

POTENTIAL anti-pattern #4 (no feature without a test) is satisfied (AT-1775/1776 cover the builtin layers + codegen). POTENTIAL honesty-principle violation only MATERIALIZES if Critical #1 (A/B fairness) or Critical #2 (tolerance loosening) is not fixed — both would be a moved goalpost.
spirv_concerns: OpFConvert f32->f16 lowering is CORRECT: it is the exact inverse of emit_f16_bits_to_f32's final OpFConvert (q4_0.rs:167, b.f_convert(f32_ty,None,f16_val)); the new helper is b.f_convert(f16_ty,None,f32_id). SPIR-V OpFConvert uses round-to-nearest-even by default; no FPRoundingMode decoration is needed or used in-tree (FPRoundingMode is only meaningful/allowed with specific capabilities and is NOT required for plain OpFConvert). Confirmed.

NO new capability: OpFConvert to/from f16 requires only Float16, ALREADY declared by shared[f16] (shared.rs:120) and coopmat-f16 (emit.rs:365). The fused kernel uses BOTH already. AT-1773's OpCapability/OpExtension set-diff vs matmul_rb_coopmat.axc is the correct proof. BUT NOTE: matmul_rb_coopmat.axc has NO Int8/StorageBuffer8BitAccess/SPV_KHR_8bit_storage — the fused kernel ADDS readonly_buffer[u8] (the q weights), which WILL pull in Int8 + StorageBuffer8BitAccess + SPV_KHR_8bit_storage (via ptr_read_u8_zext, q4_0.rs:49-50). So the AT-1773 claim 'declares NO capability/extension absent from matmul_rb_coopmat.axc' is FALSE as written — the u8 weight buffer legitimately adds 8-bit-storage caps. AT-1773 must compare against the UNION of matmul_rb_coopmat.axc AND q4km_dequant_matmul.axc capability sets (or assert 'no capability beyond Float16 + the 8bit-storage set already used by the frozen Q4_K_M dequant'), NOT against matmul_rb_coopmat.axc alone. The no-NEW-capability claim for f32_to_f16 specifically (Float16 only) is correct; the AT-1773 baseline is wrong.

f32->f16 overflow/NaN/Inf: a dequantized weight magnitude > 65504 becomes f16 +/-Inf; NaN propagates; subnormals flush per device. This is DEFINED behavior (OpFConvert), not UB. The oracle applies the identical half-crate round-trip so any such case compares equal. Acceptable AS DOCUMENTED — but confirm the half crate's f16::from_f32 saturates-to-Inf identically to the device's OpFConvert (it does for IEEE binary16; the round-trip is RNE). Low risk.
vendor_concerns: f16 coopmat accumulator precision is VENDOR-DEPENDENT: matrix[f16,16,16,accumulator] means the accumulate happens at the device's coopmat result precision. On NVIDIA tensor cores the f16-accumulator path may internally use higher precision than strict f16, which would make the f32-ref oracle pass MORE easily on NVIDIA than the spec's worst-case reasoning implies — but the WITHIN-TOL gate would then be NVIDIA-specific and could FAIL on a different vendor's strict-f16 accumulator. Since tests are NVIDIA-only (typed-skip on Lavapipe/CoopMatUnsupported, subgroup!=32), the 1e-3 pass is only proven on NVIDIA. Document that the within-tol result is NVIDIA-coopmat-accumulator-specific, not a portable guarantee.

subgroup_size()!=32 hard-skip is correct (RB structure requires wave32); matches M3.3c. AMD wave64 / Intel variable subgroups are out of scope for this NVIDIA-only kernel — acceptable for M3.5 but the thesis's AMD/Intel win remains unproven (as in M3.4).

summary: f32_to_f16 is a CORRECT, minimal, no-new-capability builtin (OpFConvert RNE, exact inverse of the existing f16_bits_to_f32 final step; SharedWriteTypeMismatch genuinely forces it). The fusion structure (frozen M2.6 dequant + frozen M3.3c RB) is sound and the perf-honesty discipline (no asserted TFLOPS, OQ-4) is good. TWO CENTRAL HOLES block APPROVE. (1) A/B FAIRNESS: the design headlines AXIOM's GEMM-TFLOPS vs llama's n==1 GEMV-TFLOPS (7.39) — and the pinned raw data proves the SAME llama kernel runs at 101 TFLOPS at n=512, so this comparison FLATTERS AXIOM by ~13x (would print 'AXIOM ahead' while same-shape shows AXIOM 4-10x behind). This is the inverse of M3.4's honest loss and MUST be reframed: the kill-criterion-of-record must be SAME-SHAPE (AXIOM GEMM vs llama n=512 GEMM), with the GEMV-boundary only as labeled context. (2) NUMERICS ORACLE: the GPU accumulator is f16 (matmul_rb_coopmat.axc:122-125) but the reference accumulates f32 — the oracle does NOT match the GPU's accumulation precision, and the 1e-3-holds-at-K<=512 claim is asserted without derivation (OQ-2 admits it is unconfirmed). The Coder must NOT loosen the FROZEN 1e-3 to pass K=512; either accumulate the reference in f16 or cap the gate-K and report larger-K divergence separately. Plus: AT-1773's no-new-capability baseline is wrong (readonly_buffer[u8] legitimately adds 8bit-storage caps absent from matmul_rb_coopmat.axc). NEEDS_REVISION: fix the A/B to same-shape, lock the tolerance + match the oracle's accumulation precision (or cap gate-K honestly), and correct AT-1773. APPROVE once those land.
